#2142. EFL expert drops ‘exciting’ West Brom promotion prediction

West Brom are positioned in 5th place in the Championship table after 15 fixtures and are in the play-offs along with Stoke City, Wolves, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR. WBA are only a point behind joint-top Birmingham City and Middlesbrough.

The Baggies beat Millwall 3-0 at The Hawthorns last time out before the international break. Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Felix Horn Myhre got their goals against the Lions as they secured another eye-catching win.

Elek has been impressed with the Midlands outfit and has delivered his verdict on the latest episode of the Not The 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They have been absolutely phenomenal in the past couple of games. They’ve gone from a team I thought are going to start well and then drop off to a relegation scrap. They’ve proven me completely wrong. In 5th place, a point off top spot. Talking about can Birmingham maintain this, can West Brom? The answer is yes. The numbers are good, the performances are good. The results are good. The players are good. It’s all looking quite exciting.”

West Brom endured a tough past campaign and churned through both Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay before they settled on James Morrison. WBA were in a relegation battle before Morrison managed to keep them up in the end.

Morrison has managed to steady the ship with the Baggies and has done a solid job. His side are now in the top eight and are eyeing the Premier League.

It was a busy summer for them and they ended up bringing in the likes of Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Barney Stewart and Rabby Nzingoula, among others, to bolster their ranks. They also cut ties with players including Alex Mowatt, Jed Wallace and Karlan Grant to help free up space and funds to pave the way for reinforcements.

West Brom opted to go for young and hungry players in the last transfer window and they now have a nice blend of youth and experience at their diposal. Morrison will get the opportunity to sign some more new faces in January if needed ahead of the second-half of this term.

As Elek has alluded to, West Brom should be considered genuine promotion contenders. WBA are solid at the back and have threats at the top end of the pitch.

In goalkeeper Max O’Leary, they have an experienced stopper who knows the league well and is a safe pair of hands. Defender George Campbell has become one of their most prized assets in defence alongside the know-how of Nat Phillips and/or Chris Mepham.

Nzingoula, Molumby and Ousmane Diakite have bags of energy in the middle of the park, whilst Horn Myhre and Price have quality to hurt opposition defenders. Up top, Morgan has a very bright future ahead of him in the game and the Baggies’ decision to sign him earlier this year was a masterstroke.

West Brom are back in action on Saturday 21st October with an away trip to Swansea City. They should be in confident mood ahead of their trek down to South Wales.

L'U.S. Sassuolo Calcio comunica di aver affidato al Sig. Roberto D'aversa la guida tecnica della Prima Squadra fino al 30 giugno 2027. #2139. The 3 summer targets Blackburn Rovers should pursue again in January, including Balazs Toth replacement

Blackburn Rovers have exceeded the expectations of many in the early stages of the 2026/27 campaign. Tony Mowbray‘s side sit 13th in the Championship after 15 games, when many expected them to be in the thick of a relegation battle.

That fate could yet await with a lot of the season left to play, but spirits are fairly high at Ewood Park. There is no hiding that the Rovers squad needs work though, with only three new summer signings failing to suitably reinforce the ranks.

New targets will be on the radar, but Blackburn Rovers identified some smart options in the summer who could be available this winter. Here, we put forward three summer targets who should be back on the radar ahead of January…

Balazs Toth has continued to resist Blackburn Rovers’ new contract efforts. It remains to be seen exactly when he leaves, but a departure seemingly awaits at some point in 2027, and the club could do with sourcing a replacement sooner rather than later.

Alex Palmer was linked with a move to Ewood Park in the last transfer window, and he could be a fine option to consider to replace Toth. The 30-year-old is out of favour at Ipswich Town under Gary O’Neil, but he is a proven Championship goalkeeper who could quickly become a dependable No. 1 for Mowbray.

Palmer is under contract until 2028 at Portman Road but given that he has not made a Premier League matchday squad this season, the Tractor Boys should not have an issue letting him go for a fairly cheap fee.

Blackburn Rovers have one of Europe’s most clinical strikers in Andri Gudjohnsen at the moment, but competition beyond him is limited. Yuki Ohashi is the only other out-and-out centre-forward, so more depth would not go amiss.

Daniel Jebbison was targeted by Rovers in the summer and a loan-to-buy deal was even agreed, but he ended up staying at Bournemouth. Given the fact that he has played only four times so far this season, the 23-year-old would benefit from a winter move elsewhere to find more game time.

The Canadian striker has Championship experience and has strong physical traits like Gudjohnsen. Jebbison is a strong finisher on both feet and Mowbray’s style of play and ability to develop players could help him hit prolific form.

Last but not least is a much-needed midfield reinforcement. Mowbray has expressed a desire to sign a new central midfielder in the winter, and someone who offers experience but has more years ahead of Sam Morsy and Adam Forshaw would be ideal.

Alan Browne fits this profile perfectly. The 31-year-old has played over 400 Championship games but showed on loan at Middlesbrough last season that he still has plenty in the tank, offering a well-rounded skillset, versatility and energy in the middle of the park.

Browne is way down the pecking order at Sunderland and out of contract next summer. It should be an easy deal for Blackburn Rovers to strike and he would instantly improve their options in midfield.

#2138. Lazio, Floriani Mussolini la foto che spalanca il rinnovo

Il terzino e il suo agente insieme alle Due Lune, vicino al centro sportivo di Formello. Attesa per la firma.

Aria di rinnovo per Romano Floriani Mussolini. A riportare l’attenzione sul futuro del terzino della Lazio è una foto pubblicata negli ultimi minutida Le Due Lune, ristorante a tinte biancocelesti a pochi passi dal centro sportivo di Formello. Nello scatto il classe 2003 è insieme al titolare del locale, Sandro Mocci, e al suo procuratore, Federico Pastorello.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La foto arriva dopo settimane di indiscrezioni sul prolungamento. Come già riportato da LazioPress.it, l’intesa prevederebbe un contratto fino al 2030 e un adeguamento dell’ingaggio, oggi stimato in circa 150 mila euro a stagione, tra i più bassi della rosa biancoceleste. Secondo Il Messaggero, la nuova cifra si aggirerebbe intorno ai 600 mila euro annui. Lo scatto con Pastorello è il nuovo indizio. La firma resta da confermare.

La svolta è arrivata alla prima giornata di Serie A. Al Dall’Ara, in Bologna-Lazio, Floriani Mussolini è entrato al 19’ del primo tempo al posto dell’infortunato Adam Marusic. Da quel momento si è preso la fascia destra ed è diventato un punto fermo per Gennaro Gattuso, che lo ha schierato dall’inizio anche nell’ultima gara contro il Napoli. Il rinnovo riconoscerebbe il peso che il terzino ha acquisito in questi primi mesi di stagione.

#2137. L'Inter perde i pezzi: dopo Bonny, si fermano anche Thuram e Stankovic. Chivu preoccupato

È un periodo clamorosamente sfortunato per l'Inter di Cristian Chivu. Neanche il tempo di festeggiare la vittoria per 2-0 contro il Como che i nerazzurri devono fare i conti con gli infortuni di Ange-Yoan Bonny, Marcus Thuram e Aleksandar Stankovic, quest'ultimi due resi noti nella giornata di martedì: con Lautaro Martinez ancora ai box, la speranza del tecnico rumeno è di recuperare almeno il Toro e un altro interprete per non rischiare di rimanere con il solo Esposito in attacco.

Thuram ha riportato una tensione al muscolo ischiocrurale destro e non sembra preoccupare più di tanto per la sfida contro l'Atalanta, in programma alla ripresa. È chiaro però che resta un po' di apprensione, soprattutto perché ogni tipo di valutazione verrà fatta solamente nei prossimi giorni ad Appiano Gentile. Situazione decisamente più seria quella di Bonny, che ha accusato un risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra e rischia 3-4 settimane di stop.

Infine c'è il caso legato a Stankovic, il quale non era sceso in campo nel match disputato a San Siro, ma si è fermato in allenamento con la Serbia a causa di una lesione al muscolo adduttore della coscia destra. I tempi di recupero saranno chiariti in seguito, ma l'ennesimo infortunio non lascia dormire sonni tranquilli all'Inter, che dovrebbe comunque riabbracciare pure Stones e Jones.

#2136. Bucchioni: “Napoli? Allegri è un allenatore in difficoltà, la squadra è usurata”

Enzo Bucchioni, giornalista, ha parlato del Napoli negli studi di Sportitalia: “Va analizzata sotto l’aspetto psicologico. Allegri è un allenatore in difficoltà, si vede anche dalla postura del corpo. Lui lo sa benissimo che ha sulle spalle l’esonero dalla Juventus, il brutale esonero dal Milan, che non ha ancora digerito e che ha dimostrato di avere ancora dentro di sè nello sfogo dopo la Roma. Ha tirato in ballo, guarda caso, il Milan, perché è qualcosa che si porta ancora dentro. Va nello spogliatoio, gli succede un’altra cosa, viene contestato e cosa dice a se stesso? «Sono ancora il più forte». Quasi come se volesse sentirselo dire da fuori, ma se lo dice da solo per caricarsi. un posto dopo quell’esonero che comunque gli brucia ancora sulla pelle. Questa è la prima cosa. Dal punto di vista calcistico, torno a quello che diceva Credendino, perché tutto è nato da lì. Quando Antonio Conte mi dice: «Io non parteciperò a un funerale, non accompagno il morto», quella frase andava analizzata, non come una battuta sul fatto che Conte frequenta un ristorante da cento euro, come fece… Lui ha voluto dire una cosa ben precisa: questa squadra è usurata. E’ usurata da due Scudetti, molti giocatori sono gli stessi, è usurata dal punto di vista fisico, è vecchia e andava cambiata profondamente”.

#2135. ‘Definitely’: EFL expert has say on Birmingham City’s top two chances

Birmingham City are sat top of the Championship table after their first 15 fixtures of the season. BCFC are above Middlesbrough and Stoke City on goal difference, with the likes of Wolves, West Brom and Swansea City also chasing them down.

The Blues are back in action after the international break with an away trip to the Bet365 Stadium to take on Stoke City as they aim to keep their momentum going. They beat Swansea City 2-1 at home last time out after a brace by Jay Stansfield.

Elek reckons the Midlands outfit can keep it up and has said on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They can definitely stay there. There is no reason why they can’t. We’re not talking about a Championship minnow here. We’re talking about a club who have invested a lot of money in their playing squad. They were the best League One squad vs the level we’ve seen in a long time.”

He added: “The ascent Ipswich and Sunderland have shown, and to an extent Coventry although that took a few more seasons, the pathway is already there.”

Birmingham City came up from League One back in 2025 after they stormed to the title. BCFC then spent the last campaign adapting to life in the Championship and fell short of the play-offs.

The Blues stuck with head coach Chris Davies in the summer though and that decision has worked out well for them. They are rock solid at the back and they have the best defensive record in the division at the moment ahead of West Brom and Southampton.

Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann have both been excellent at the heart of defence, with Alex Cochrane to the left of them. Dael Fry, who joined in the summer after the end of his contract at Middlesbrough, then provides useful back-up from the bench.

Further up the pitch, Jhon Solis, Paik Seung-ho and Tomoki Iwata inject quality into their midfield department. Stansfield, Liam Millar, Patrick Roberts, Demarai Gray and August Priske are all dangerous attackers and can cause serious issues to opposition defenders.

Birmingham City could do with another striker in the January transfer window. BCFC need some competition for Priske with Luis Vazquez struggling to get to grips with English football.

The Blues would also benefit from another attacking midfielder or winger ahead of the second-half of the season. Their pursuit of Joe Gelhardt in the summer was well documented and someone like him would be ideal, although he won’t leave Hull City.

You could also argue that Davies should bring in another central defender this winter too. If Klarer, Neumann or Fry were to get injured, they would be left pretty short of depth in that area.

Birmingham City are on a roll and will be full of confidence. Coventry City and Hull City showed last season that you don’t need parachute payments to go up.

The Blues need to stay grounded though and can’t get too carried away. Their away defeat at Cardiff City last month proved every single match is tough.

#2134. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 10 novembre

INTER, CALHANOGLU PUÒ RINNOVARE. LAVORI IN CORSO PER IL NUOVO ACCORDO CON THURAM. CISSE RIMANE AL MILAN, RIFIUTATE DUE PROPOSTE. COMO, IDEA MALO GUSTO CON I BUONI RAPPORTI INSIEME AL CHELSEA. JUVENTUS, NON BASTANO GLI ATTACCANTI CHE HA SPALLETTI: PENSIERO FISSO CON SORLOTH. TUTTI GLI OBIETTIVI DEL NAPOLI PER RIPARTIRE A GENNAIO, ALLEGRI HA UNA PRIORITÀ. ROMA, ENDRICK CHIODO FISSO E SPUNTA BALDE COME IDEA DEL MERCATO INVERNALE.

Il tema del rinnovo di contratto di Hakan Calhanoglu è tornato improvvisamente d'attualità in casa Inter, la volontà comune è quella di proseguire insieme e tentare di chiudere l'accordo al più presto, persino entro Natale se si incastreranno tutti i tasselli. Si tratta di un segnale distensivo fondamentale dopo un periodo turbolento iniziato ad agosto: durante la tournée australiana, infatti, il centrocampista turco aveva manifestato qualche perplessità sulla mancanza di contatti per il prolungamento e il timore di non essere più considerato centrale nelle strategie del club, pur ribadendo il forte legame con Milano, l'Inter e i tifosi e forte della fiducia incondizionata del tecnico Cristian Chivu. Ritrovata la serenità ed eseguito il primo passo con la riapertura del dialogo, il vero nodo resta tuttavia di natura economica. Attualmente legato ai nerazzurri fino al 2027 a circa 6,5 milioni netti a stagione, Calhanoglu punta a un nuovo biennale con un ingaggio da top player; dal canto suo, la società mira a ridurre la quota fissa degli stipendi tenendo conto dell'età e dei recenti guai fisici del classe '94. La trattativa rimane dunque aperta e richiederà la giusta intesa tra le parti per arrivare alla fumata bianca.

In casa Inter si lavora per blindare Marcus Thuram: il club nerazzurro ha infatti avviato i primi contatti per prolungare l'accordo con l'attaccante francese, attualmente in scadenza nel 2028, con l'obiettivo di estenderlo fino al 2031. La trattativa si preannuncia tuttavia in salita per motivi economici: la società guidata in panchina da Cristian Chivu vorrebbe proporre una ristrutturazione dell'ingaggio basata su una quota fissa da 4,5-5 milioni di euro integrata da premi e benefit, a fronte dello stipendio attuale da 6,5 milioni che con i bonus sfiora gli 8 milioni a stagione. Una formula che per ora non convince la punta, decisa a non ridimensionare le proprie condizioni contrattuali pur ribadendo la priorità assoluta di vestire la maglia dell'Inter, pur in presenza dei fari puntati da diversi club esteri per l'estate. La forte spinta dei dirigenti verso il rinnovo è legata a doppio filo al rendimento sul campo: dall'infortunio di Lautaro Martinez, Thuram si è preso il peso dell'attacco collezionando quattro gol e due assist in sei gare di campionato, confermandosi elemento imprescindibile nello scacchiere tattico nerazzurro.

Alphadjo Cisse non ha nascosto l'entusiasmo per il suo travolgente inizio di stagione con la maglia del Milan: l'attaccante rossonero ha confidato come la tripletta messa a segno in Europa League sia stata la conferma di poter stare a questi livelli, vivendola non come un punto d'arrivo ma come una promessa mantenuta al bambino che era, consapevole dei propri mezzi e molto esigente con se stesso nonostante il recente lungo infortunio e la giovane età. Una fiducia ricambiata appieno dalla società di via Aldo Rossi che, a pochi mesi dall'arrivo del giocatore, è già al lavoro con i suoi agenti per blindarlo e respingere le sirene di mercato, in particolare quelle del Brighton che sta bussando alla porta con offerte milionarie: l'obiettivo del Milan è infatti quello di adeguare le condizioni contrattuali di Cisse, portando l'ingaggio attuale da circa 800 mila euro al doppio e prolungando la scadenza oltre l'attuale termine del 30 giugno 2030.

Il Como potrebbe inserirsi nella corsa per Malo Gusto: il club lariano, rivelazione della Champions League, avrebbe messo nel mirino il terzino destro classe 2003 del Chelsea, il quale sarebbe pronto a valutare un cambio di scenario nella prossima finestra di mercato pur di trovare più spazio in prima squadra e difendere il proprio ruolo centrale in ottica nazionale francese. Dal canto loro, i Blues non avrebbero chiuso la porta a un addio già a gennaio, complice una discontinuità testimoniata dalle zero presenze da titolare nelle ultime sei uscite di Premier League per l'ex Lione, arrivato a Londra nel 2023. Per accaparrarsi il talento transalpino, apprezzato per giovane età, spinta sulla fascia e ampi margini di crescita, il Como dovrà tuttavia superare la agguerrita concorrenza internazionale di Atletico Madrid, Milan e Lipsia, pronte a scatenare un'asta qualora i dirigenti inglesi aprano definitivamente alla cessione a titolo definitivo o in prestito.

La Juventus continua a valutare opzioni per il mercato di riparazione di gennaio ed è pronta a tornare alla carica per Alexander Sorloth: nonostante i lievi segnali di crescita mostrati da Nick Woltemade e Randal Kolo Muani, i bianconeri intendono regalare al tecnico Luciano Spalletti una punta forte fisicamente e abile ad attaccare la profondità, riallacciando i contatti per il centravanti norvegese dell'Atletico Madrid già concretamente seguito a giugno con un viaggio in Norvegia del direttore sportivo Marco Ottolini. Pur apprezzato da Diego Simeone dopo aver superato i guai fisici di inizio stagione, l'attaccante ex Lipsia non è considerato intoccabile dai Colchoneros e vorrebbe maggior spazio; forte degli ottimi rapporti tra i club - e con la posizione di Jonathan David, attualmente a Madrid in prestito dalla Juve, che potrebbe incidere nelle dinamiche -, la società torinese mantiene attiva la pista, pur monitorando profili alternativi come Gianluca Scamacca, Mateo Retegui e Folarin Balogun, quest'ultimo già proposto in estate da Jorge Mendes.

Il Napoli ha già iniziato a pianificare le strategie per la sessione invernale di calciomercato: la dirigenza azzurra è al lavoro per mettere a disposizione del tecnico Massimiliano Allegri quattro rinforzi mirati - nello specifico un centravanti, un esterno d'attacco e due centrocampisti -, un piano che potrebbe essere accompagnato anche da alcune uscite per ridisegnare l'organico in vista della seconda parte di stagione. Per l'attacco il profilo in cima alle preferenze è quello del ventunenne Gustavo Varela, protagonista di un avvio di campionato straordinario con la maglia del Monza che lo vede guidare la classifica marcatori di Serie A con nove reti (undici totali in stagione) ed essere premiato con la chiamata della nazionale portoghese, mentre sull'esterno resta vivo l'interesse per il ventiduenne Jamie Bynoe-Gittens, in uscita dal Chelsea e gradito anche per questioni di lista. Infine, per il reparto mediano i fari sono puntati sul giovane talento del Sassuolo Darryl Bakola, che compirà 19 anni a fine novembre, ma il vero sogno e priorità assoluta rimane Mamadou Coulibaly, classe 2004 del Monaco, per il quale tuttavia la valutazione di circa 40 milioni di euro pretesa dai francesi rende la trattativa assai complessa pur senza scoraggiare i dirigenti partenopei.

Il futuro di Endrick al Real Madrid si trova a un bivio in vista della sessione invernale di calciomercato: il ventenne, attaccante brasiliano, sta valutando seriamente di lasciare i blancos a gennaio per ritrovare continuità ed evitare di rallentare la propria crescita. Nonostante l'ottimo rapporto con José Mourinho, che in estate ne aveva bloccato il trasferimento alla Roma, la punta ha collezionato soltanto 140 minuti spalmati su 7 presenze, ripercorrendo l'inizio della scorsa stagione prima che il prestito al Lione gli permettesse di esplodere con 8 gol e 7 assist in 21 gare e conquistare la chiamata al Mondiale con la Seleçao del CT Carlo Ancelotti. Sulle sue tracce resta vigile la Roma, ma la concorrenza più agguerrita è quella dello Sporting guidato proprio da Paulo Fonseca, il tecnico che lo aveva valorizzato in Francia e che saprebbe offrirgli garanzie d'impiego, la vetrina della Champions League e un ambientamento facilitato dalla lingua; dal canto suo, la dirigenza del Real Madrid non intende ostacolare la partenza per tutelare un investimento superiore agli 80 milioni ed evitare svalutazioni, mentre dal ritiro del Brasile lo stesso Endrick ha ribadito con maturo affetto la propria priorità, dichiarando di apprezzare la vicinanza umana di Mourinho ma di voler solo giocare e dare un reale impulso alla propria carriera.

In casa Roma l'avvio di campionato ha certificato ambizioni da scudetto: dopo undici giornate la squadra ha dimostrato di avere i numeri per lottare fino in fondo e la finestra invernale di calciomercato rappresenta l'occasione perfetta per puntellare la rosa a disposizione di Gian Piero Gasperini con un paio di innesti di spessore. Tra i profili finiti nel mirino del direttore sportivo Tony D’Amico c'è Alejandro Balde, esterno sinistro classe 2003 in forza al Barcellona; il club catalano potrebbe aprire alla cessione già a gennaio per fare cassa e investire su un difensore centrale, vera priorità del tecnico Hansi Flick. Incassato il pieno gradimento di Gasperini, lo scoglio principale per i giallorossi rimane la formula dell'operazione - con l'ipotesi di un prestito oneroso con obbligo di riscatto condizionato alla qualificazione in Champions League -, resa complessa da un'alta valutazione del cartellino e da un ingaggio di rilievo. A complicare ulteriormente i piani della Roma c'è poi l'affollata concorrenza internazionale scatenata dall'apertura dei blaugrana: in Premier League si muovono Liverpool, Aston Villa, Manchester United, Manchester City e Tottenham, in Ligue 1 c'è il Monaco, mentre in Italia anche la Juventus valuta l'opzione nell'eventualità di un addio di Andrea Cambiaso, rendendo il terzino spagnolo uno dei pezzi pregiati più contesi della imminente sessione di mercato.

ANTONIO CONTE SORPRENDE: PROCURA A ZAHAVI, VUOLE LO UNITED. LINDELOF RINNOVA CON L'ASTON VILLA, MANCA SOLO L'UFFICIALITÀ PER L'ESONERO DI CAHUZAC DAL LENS, VAN DIJK NON PENSA AL FUTURO PER ORA.

La panchina di Michael Carrick al Manchester United appare ormai sul punto di crollare: secondo le ultime indiscrezioni, l'esonero del tecnico inglese è considerato una semplice questione di tempo nei prossimi giorni, dato che il rocambolesco 4-4 strappato in extremis a Old Trafford contro l'Aston Villa non è bastato a raddrizzare la rotta né a sanare il feeling incrinato con lo spogliatoio. Mentre le quotazioni di Mauricio Pochettino continuavano a salire - con l'attuale commissario tecnico degli Stati Uniti che avrebbe già dato la propria disponibilità a raccogliere il testimone, forte di una clausola rescissoria da 9 milioni di euro per liberarsi dal contratto fino al 2030 con la selezione americana e di una residenza familiare a Londra -, il quadro si è improvvisamente complicato con l'inserimento a sorpresa di Antonio Conte. Il 57enne, allenatore leccese, libero dopo l'addio al Napoli a fine scorsa stagione, si sarebbe infatti affidato al potente agente Pini Zahavi con l'obiettivo specifico di farsi avanti per la guida dei Red Devils; in attesa di capire se la dirigenza di Old Trafford affonderà il colpo prima del doppio impegno di Pochettino nei quarti di Concacaf Nations League contro Haiti, la corsa alla successione di Carrick resta più intricata che mai.

L'Aston Villa blinda Victor Lindelof. Il club inglese ha annunciato di aver esercitato l'opzione presente nel contratto del difensore svedese, prolungando l'accordo fino al 2028. Arrivato a Villa Park nel 2025, l'ex Manchester United ha avuto un impatto immediato, diventando uno dei punti di riferimento della squadra. Nel suo primo anno con la maglia dei Villans è stato protagonista anche nella conquista dell'Europa League, giocando un ruolo importante nella finale vinta 3-0 contro il Friburgo a Istanbul. Lindelöf ha finora disputato 43 partite con la maglia dell'Aston Villa e si è rapidamente affermato al centro della difesa grazie alla sua esperienza e alla capacità di guidare il reparto arretrato. Il classe 1994 continua inoltre a essere anche un elemento fondamentale della nazionale svedese, di cui è il capitano. Con il rinnovo fino al 2028, il club di Birmingham conferma la volontà di puntare ancora sulle sue qualità.

Il Lens si appresta a cambiare nuovamente guida tecnica: nelle prossime ore la società francese ufficializzerà l'esonero di Yannick Cahuzac, maturato dopo la riunione dirigenziale di lunedì sera e motivato da un avvio di stagione condellato da risultati deludenti e devastanti sul piano psicologico. Figura emblematica del club, Cahuzac lascerà definitivamente i Sang et Or senza essere ricollocato in altri ruoli societari dopo un'avventura durata appena due mesi: subentrato il 21 settembre a Dino Toppmoller in seguito al ko con il Monaco (1-2), il tecnico ha visto segnato il proprio destino dal recente k.o. interno contro il Marsiglia (1-2), arrivato a pochi giorni dal pesantissimo 1-9 incassato in Champions League contro il Como, sconfitta che rappresenta la peggiore di sempre per una squadra transalpina nelle coppe europee. Per la successione la dirigenza sta valutando tre profili e tra questi spunta la clamorosa candidatura di Pierre Sage: andato via in estate, l'ex allenatore si trova attualmente in bilico sulla panchina del Crystal Palace, con un esonero imminente in Premier League che potrebbe trasformarlo nella soluzione immediata per restituire stabilità all'ambiente.

Virgil van Dijk non teme di finire in scadenza con il Liverpool al termine della stagione, nonostante i suoi 35 anni. "Se si prolunga, tanto meglio. Altrimenti, andrò altrove. Non c'è nulla da segnalare per il momento, ma questo non significa che sono in panico. Mentalmente sto bene; fisicamente ho avuto un piccolo problema in queste ultime due settimane, ma sto facendo tutto il possibile per essere presente sul campo". Qualsiasi possibilità per il difensore olandese, che a parametro zero farebbe certamente gola a chiunque.

#2133. Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

Little sorcerer calls time on playing for his country six weeks after World Cup final defeat which was marred by brutality of his team-mates

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

#2131. QPR’s Top 3 players of the 2026/27 season so far, including resurgent 6-goal/assist star

QPR sit 8th in the Championship table with the latest international break upon us. The Hoops have had some patchy form in recent weeks, but they enter the break off the back of a 2-1 win over Lincoln City.

Julien Stephan and co will be pleased with their efforts to date, but there’s room for improvement. The time without league football offers the R’s a chance to put some work in on the training ground, while we can assess the season so far and pick out some standout stars.

In no particular order, we put forward QPR’s top three players of the 2026/27 season so far…

Ronnie Edwards’ fine loan at QPR in the 2024/25 season meant they knew what to expect when he returned permanently earlier this year. He reclaimed a key role swiftly, and the 23-year-old has gone from strength to strength this term.

Used in defensive midfield and centre-back by Stephan, Edwards is one of the Hoops’ most influential players. As per FotMob‘s data, he stands out in possession as he ranks among the Championship’s best centre-backs for successful passes (767), long ball completion rate (62.1%), interceptions (20) and recoveries (65).

His best displays include the big home wins over Swansea City and Derby County, and the 0-0 draw at Charlton Athletic. Edwards has been consistent all season though, proving his star quality at this level.

Throughout his second stint at QPR, Paul Smyth has endured some tough spells. After three years, some may have expected the Northern Irishman to be phased out of the first XI by the likes of Harvey Vale, Karamoko Dembele, Kwame Poku or Koki Saito, but that has not been the case.

Smyth has retained a regular role in Stephan’s side, and it is not hard to see why. The resurgent 29-year-old shows the commitment and endeavour Stephan desires from his attackers, and he’s added more end product to his game with three goals and three assists in his 14 league appearances this season.

He is tied with Richard Kone at the top of the goal contribution charts at Loftus Road and ranks in the top three of Hoops players for big chances created (3), xG on target (2.0) and expected assists (1.6). Smyth has also won three penalties – more than any other player in the Championship (FotMob).

Last but not least is Pierce Charles, whose influence from goalkeeper cannot be overrstated. The Northern Irish prospect arrived as a highly-regarded talent on loan from Manchester City after his Sheffield Wednesday breakthrough, and he has not disappointed.

Charles has work to do with his shot-stopping, as shown by an xG prevented of -2.47 and a save percentage of 67.9%. However, he makes this list because of how his abilities with the ball have changed the way QPR play.

His distribution ability makes Stephan’s side so much more comfortable at the back and they have more routes to the attack thanks to his range of passing. No Championship goalkeeper has made more than his 564 successful passes (FotMob) and he has fantastic numbers in his pass completion rate (77.7%) and long pass accuracy (46.6%).

It has been a real team effort from QPR to start the season in strong fashion. There were some impressive performers overlooked for inclusion here.

Captain Jimmy Dunne has been key with his physical presence and leadership from the back. Midfielder Glen Kamara has made a positive impact since his arrival as well, and if he continues in his recent form, he will be firmly in the player of the season conversation at Loftus Road.

Ilias Chair and Boy Kemper deserve early mentions too, but injuries have limited their involvement compared to others. Kealey Adamson has been one of the most improved players when stepping in at full-back for the R’s.

#2130. Emergenza Inter, tutti i perché: non c'è un nuovo Pio Esposito ed è costruita per un solo modulo (poco europeo). L'Under 23 ancora non produce e il mercato sta prendendo una direzione diversa

Piove sul bagnato per l'Inter che dopo Ange-Yoan Bonny per circa un mese, perde pure Marcus Thuram. I due si sono fermati dopo l'ultima partita contro il Como e hanno dovuto lasciare i rispettivi ritiri di Costa d'Avorio e Francia. Non solo: Lautaro Martinez tornerà a lavorare pienamente col gruppo solo pochi giorni prima del prossimo impegno contro l'Atalanta e Christian Chivu fa ogni tipo di scongiuro affinché Francesco Pio Esposito torni integro ad Appiano Gentile dopo il doppio (e intenso) impegno con la Nazionale. Le ultime su Thuram dicono che potrebbe essere solo un affaticamento, ma ciò non toglie che la coperta resti corta...

Quattro uomini e due maglie, per un attacco a due punte, è una coperta non corta, non lunga. 'Giusta', verrebbe da dire, ma solo se alle spalle dei giocatori che hai in rosa, in un calcio dal calendario frenetico e così intenso, hai dei giovani pronti. Mattia Mosconi è un esterno di grandissimo talento, un sottopunta che si sta facendo le ossa (è un 2007) tra Primavera e soprattutto Serie C con l'Under 23. Un progetto all'inizio, quello nerazzurro, che per adesso non ha ponti e collegamenti con la prima squadra. Matteo Lavelli è più puntero, più 'Pio' che dieci/undici. In C ha fatto un gol, coi grandi di Chivu s'è visto a sprazzi. E questo è il primo problema (lui è un 2006): da quando l'Inter ha strutturato la seconda squadra, ancora non ci sono calciatori che come ai tempi della Juventus Next Gen siano stati cresciuti e formati per essere subito pronti per i grandi. Sarà questa l'occasione, tra necessità e virtù? Certo è che non c'è un Pio Esposito, visto che mancano i giocatori (come anche Alphadjo Cissè al Milan) che abbiano fatto esperienza in Serie B.

Altro problema. L'Inter è una rosa costruita per vincere in Italia, che ha grandi campioni, che ha un'identità straordinaria. Però negli ultimi tre anni in particolare, il pallone sta prendendo una direzione diversa. E i nerazzurri sono una delle squadre che meno di tutte in Europa saltano l'uomo, che cercano meno il dribbling. Ha una rosa costruita con una sola identità, il 3-5-2, il binario d'Inzaghiana memoria e prima ancora di Contiana tradizione. E su quello (ottimamente) marcia, spedita. Solo che non sta trovando un'alternativa di strategia tattica. Il tentativo maldestro di Chivu nel Derby col Milan lo racconta. In Europa si gioca a quattro dietro e con uomini capaci di creare la superiorità davanti. L'Inter è meravigliosamente preparata ma è abbastanza? Questo, in situazioni d'emergenza, soprattutto in difesa e in attacco, crea dei problemi. Perché non è duttile, perché è rigida, perché è dogmatica e non fluida come il calcio d'oggi imporrebbe. E invece no. E invece nella sfortuna deve più pregare che trovare soluzioni alternative, o cercare giovani che però sta aspettando piuttosto che costruendo con rapidità.

#2129. Candreva e la Lazio: «non ho mai rifiutato» il ruolo di vicecapitano

Pioli gli propose l’incarico in camera; l’ex giocatore ricorda anche l’accoglienza dei tifosi dopo il gol al San Paolo.

Antonio Candreva non ha mai rifiutato di diventare vicecapitano della Lazio. L’ex biancoceleste lo ha chiarito a Crazy Calcio Show, ripercorrendo anche il rapporto con i tifosi e la notte trascorsa senza dormire prima della finale di Coppa Italia contro la Roma. Oggi fa parte dello staff tecnico della Nazionale Under 15.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Candreva ricorda i quattro anni e mezzo alla Lazio come un’esperienza indimenticabile. L’inizio, però, non fu semplice: pesava su di lui una presunta fede romanista. Il gol segnato al San Paolo contro il Napoli segnò una svolta nel rapporto con i sostenitori biancocelesti.

«Quello è stato il momento in cui sono stato accolto dalla Lazio», ha raccontato. Candreva descrive quell’avvicinamento come qualcosa voluto sia da lui sia dal pubblico, una liberazione. Ha aggiunto che la curva biancoceleste era quella capace di dargli più carica in campo e che ancora oggi è felice di aver ricevuto un coro dai tifosi.

L’ex giocatore ha poi smentito la ricostruzione secondo cui avrebbe rinunciato a fare il vicecapitano quando la fascia passò sul braccio di Biglia. «È una storia falsa, perché non pretendevo nulla», ha precisato. Davanti a lui, ha ricordato, c’erano giocatori come Radu, Marchetti e Klose: per questo non si aspettava alcun incarico.

Quando Pioli lo chiamò in camera per proporgli il ruolo, la questione fu discussa insieme. Candreva ha ribadito il punto con parole nette: «non ho mai rifiutato».

#2128. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

Today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the new players, to build our team to get their best today.

I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

She wore… she wore… she wore a yellow ribbon …

Two changes – Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson make debuts. Joao Gomes misses the match as the first of his three-game suspension and Marco Bizot drops to the bench.

Double debuts 🤩Your Villa XI to face Arsenal this evening 👋 pic.twitter.com/Zue0ZTSJt9

Arteta names unchanged starting XI but Bruno Guimaraes is fit for the bench. Ezri Konsa joins him there.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵Unchanged for Monday night football 🔐🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/ptvpKHDahn

In its rightful place 🏠🏆 pic.twitter.com/FMH4zve1aD

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#2127. Napoli, Bianchini: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand”

Tommaso Bianchini, direttore Generale dell’Area Business della SSC Napoli, ha partecipato al panel “Club, non solo Squadre”, nell’ambito dell’edizione 2026 del Social Football Summit, in corso all’Allianz Stadium di Torino. Nel corso del suo intervento, Bianchini ha ripercorso il processo di ideazione e realizzazione del progetto del Centenario: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand e sviluppare relazioni con partner internazionali che hanno riconosciuto in SSC Napoli un canale privilegiato per entrare in contatto con milioni di tifosi e appassionati in tutto il mondo. La sfida per il futuro è accelerare ulteriormente questo percorso attraverso la creazione di una piattaforma di marketing integrata, capace di rafforzare il posizionamento globale del Club e sviluppare nuove forme di collaborazione con i nostri partner”.

#2126. Delio Rossi: “ Gattuso ha trasformato la negatività in positività”

Ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, è intervenuto Delio Rossi

Ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, è intervenuto Delio Rossi per commentare le ultime vicende di Casa Lazio e svelare alcuni retroscena.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Quando è arrivato Gattuso tutti pensavano che non fosse consono. Io l'ho portato in Italia e l'ho allenato. Ha una grande sensibilità calcistica e soprattutto ha grande orgoglio. Ero convinto potesse fare bene. Gattuso ha trasformato la negatività in positività. C'era tanto scetticismo nei suoi confronti e nei confronti dei suoi giocatori. Lui gli è entrato nella testa e li ha spinti a dimostrare che sono del livello Lazio, senza piangersi addosso. Ha cercato dei nemici e contro di questi ha coalizzato lasquadra. Poi c'è la condizione atletica, fondamentale per praticare quel tipo di gioco.

No, era più un'indiscrezione giornalistica, non avevamo il potenziale per acquistarlo. Io avevo chiesto un centro-mediano metodista e un centravanti, due argentini che non era di grido ma che rendevano la squadra più organica. Walter Sabatini se ne prese la responsabilità, aveva detto che era pronto a dimettersi, ma alla fine lo convinsi a non farlo.

La vita mi ha portato da altre parti, ma avrei voluto lavorare con i ragazzi. Penso di essere indicato. Secondo me in futuro avranno un ruolo centrale l'alimentazione, l'aspetto psicologico e il miglioramento sulle carenze. Giocando ogni tre giorni servirà reiterare nel tempo la preparazione atletica. Io lavorerei sempre sul singolo, ma significherebbe lavorare 4/5 ore a settimana. Se mi chiamasse Lotito? Un problema che non esiste

#2124. Watford hold talks with 48-year-old boss who has been out of work since October 2025

Watford are sat 20th in the Championship table with 15 points from as many games. The Hornets have struggled for any sort of momentum, putting pressure on manager Alessio Dionisi despite the club hierarchy’s reported desire to give the boss more time than some of his predecessors.

Now though, a report from Romanian journalist Emanuel Rose states Watford have held talks with Edward Iordanescu over the managerial position at Vicarage Road. Contact has been described as ‘positive’, but there have not been any concrete English reports that the Championship side are considering a managerial change.

Iordanescu is available having been out of the game since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025. He previously managed Romania’s national team, alongside prestigious clubs such as FCSB and CFR Cluj.

Iordanescu is a 48-year-old coach who started his career in the dugout in 2010 after retiring in 2004. He was only 32 when he was first named as interim manager of Steaua Bucharest, where he stayed as an assistant coach to Ilie Stan until 2012.

He spent short spells in charge of Fortuna Brazi and FCM Targu Mures in Romania before first earning acclaim at Pandurii Targu Jiu, where his work earned him the CSKA Sofia job in Bulgaria. That stint lasted only 12 games though, and Iordanescu would return to his native in spells at Astra Giurgiu, CFR Cluj (x2), Gaz Metan and FCSB.

The rumoured Watford target managed the Romania national side from January 2022 to July 2024, winning 10 of 28 games and leading them to the UEFA Euro 2024 round of 16 before leaving at the end of the tournament.

A return to club football followed at Legia Warsaw in Poland, but they struggled in European and domestic football with Iordanescu criticised for inconsistent team selection, fruitless tactical changes, poor physical output metrics and disenchantment within the squad.

Iordanescu won the Romanian Superliga once and their Super Cup twice, and the same trophy in Poland once. His most used formation is a 4-3-3, but has also deployed his sides in a 4-2-3-1 setup.

As touched on earlier, nothing has been concretely reported by English or local outlets that Watford are planning a change in the dugout. However, rumoured talks with Iordanescu could indicate that they are staying prepared if they do sack Dionisi at the very leasy.

If there is a time to change manager, it is now. The international break offers a chance to get a new boss in and settled before the return to league action.

Iordanescu could be brought in swiftly and given time on the training ground to work with his new squad before club football returns against Sheffield United on November 21st. However, it remains to be seen if anything comes of the links, with managerial speculation never far around the corner at Vicarage Road.

#2123. I tifosi della Lazio chiedono il rinnovo di Danilo Cataldi

Sotto l’ultimo post ufficiale della Lazio, i tifosi chiedono al club di prolungare il contratto del centrocampista.

Sotto l’ultimo post pubblicato dal profilo ufficiale della Lazio, dove si ufficializzava il rinnovo di Floriani Mussolininfino al 2031, molti tifosi biancocelesti hanno rivolto la stessa richiesta alla società. Vogliono che Danilo Cataldi resti e che il club gli rinnovi il contratto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

«Rinnovate #Cataldi» e «Ora Danilo» sono due dei messaggi comparsi nei commenti. Due formule diverse per esprimere lo stesso desiderio, quello di continuare a vedere il centrocampista con la maglia biancoceleste.

I messaggi raccontano l’affetto per un giocatore diventato un punto di riferimento dentro e fuori dal campo. La richiesta dei tifosi è rivolta alla società, a cui spetta la decisione sul futuro del centrocampista.
